ClientResponses.Response:
Brian, we can understand how surprising this has been, especially after years of great experiences with your previous grill and the amount of time you’ve already invested trying to get this one dialed in.
We also reviewed the cook data and your contact history, and part of the temperature movement can be explained by lid openings and frequent temperature adjustments during the cook. Each time the lid is opened, heat escapes, and the grill responds by increasing fuel and airflow to recover, which can lead to temporary overshoots. In the same way, frequent changes to the set temperature prompt the system to continuously adjust, which can create visible swings as it works to stabilize. That said, these types of overshoots are typically brief and should settle into a tighter range once the grill stabilizes. The sustained fluctuations you’re describing throughout the cook go beyond what we would expect from normal recovery behavior.

If you’d like to go deeper into any of these points with or review your cook data together in more detail, you’re always welcome to reach out to us again. We’re here and happy to help.

Results.ReviewText:
I’d like to preface this review with a little background on our experience with Traeger grills. We've had a Traeger Timberline 850 for 7 years, and we loved it so much that we bought two additional grills for our children. As our family grew, we needed more grilling space than the Timberline 850 could provide, so this past winter, we replaced it with the new Timberline XL.

Unfortunately, this new grill has been unable to maintain a consistent grilling temperature. The temperature fluctuates between 45–50°F, swinging from too hot to too cold. On one occasion, it even shut down due to excessive heat. I called customer service, and after a two-hour call, they determined we had a faulty thermocouple. They sent us a replacement, but the issue persisted, prompting another call.

During this second call, customer service determined that we needed an entirely new hopper assembly. The new hopper arrived and was installed, but the problem remained.

At this point, I had spent many hours on the phone and replaced several parts. Keep in mind, this grill cost us $4,000. I called customer service again to inquire about an exchange. This call lasted the entire afternoon. I went through the troubleshooting steps again, but because I was inquiring about an exchange this time I was told that the 45-degree fluctuations were within the normal range for this model. The tone of the conversation shifted after I asked about an exchange. I was also told that there had been a mistake in diagnosing the problem earlier, which led to the incorrect parts being sent.

However, during this call, they sent me a link to their official document that states, “Your grill should fluctuate no more than ±25 degrees”, which directly contradicted what I was being told.

I then asked to speak with the manager of the representative I’d been speaking with. When I spoke to him, I was again told that a 45-degree fluctuation was normal for this model. When I asked where this was documented, he admitted that it wasn’t. The next person I spoke with was his manager, who told me that the previous information was incorrect, that the fluctuations I was experiencing were due to an “overshoot,” and that I should never open the grill during a cook. I know that an overshoot doesn’t cause a constant 45-degree fluctuation above and below the set temperature for the entire duration of a cook.

Throughout this entire call, which stretched from afternoon into evening, I was given multiple excuses for why I was experiencing this issue. By the end, I felt like I was dealing with scammers, and this whole support experience has significantly diminished my perception of the Traeger brand.

Had I not previously owned a Traeger grill and been familiar with the brand’s quality, I would have been attempting a return instead of requesting an exchange
Results.Title: Grill fluctuates 45°; poor customer service.

Results.ReviewText: The Traeger Timberline XL has been nothing but trouble from the start. If you want to spend endless hours with customer support trying to get your grill to work, then this is the grill for you. First the firebox started on fire and burned the electrical cords. Traeger sent new parts, and I installed. After using for almost a year, we got an error that said "ignitor not detected." Traeger told me it was because the grill needed an update. In order to update, I need an Internet connection which should be simple since the grill had already been connected to my Internet. Every other appliance and light and security system in my home has been able to connect, but suddenly not this grill. We've shut down the 5 ghz band, created a special guest 2.4 ghz band, bought a 50 foot ethernet cable to pretty much put the router on top of the grill, turned off the Iphone relay setting, and completed every test every customer service rep has suggested. The last suggestion was that I needed to disconnect every device connected to my Internet except the grill. Google this problem, and you'll see hundreds of other users with the same issue. It's been over a year since I could use my four thousand dollar grill. Don't waste your time or money. We have been Traeger fans from the beginning and have purchased other grills, but this purchase will be our last.

I cook 90% of my meals on the grill, all year long here in vegas. I regret this purchase so much! Save yourself the headache, and heartbreak... buy something else.

Results.ReviewText:
Traeger
I desperately wanted to love my Traeger Timberline, but it’s been an infuriating letdown. This $3,300 grill, hyped as a premium outdoor cooking masterpiece, has been a glorified lawn ornament for nearly a month due to a defective igniter. The first replacement igniter Traeger sent was also dead on arrival, doubling my frustration. A second replacement was promised before the weekend to salvage my plans, but Traeger’s hollow promises fell through—both parts are now expected after a maddening 10-day wait, with no option for expedited shipping.
Beyond my experience, other Timberline owners report a litany of issues that make this grill’s premium price tag feel like a cruel joke. Many complain of wildly inaccurate temperature controls, with some grills running over 100 degrees off the set point, rendering precise cooking impossible. Wireless meat probes frequently malfunction or fail to connect, leaving users to rely on third-party thermometers. Grease management is another sore point—poor drainage design leads to dangerous grease fires, with some users reporting flames shooting up the auger into the pellet hopper. WiFi connectivity, a touted feature, is notoriously unreliable, with the Traeger app often failing to sync or dropping connections mid-cook. Worst of all, Traeger’s customer service is consistently described as unresponsive, forcing owners to troubleshoot complex repairs themselves or wait weeks for parts, if they’re addressed at all.
My grill hasn’t been functional long enough to encounter these additional headaches, but given Traeger’s track record, I’m bracing for more disappointment. For a grill priced like a luxury car, I expected flawless performance and top-notch support. Instead, Traeger delivers a product that fails within 30 days and a customer service experience reminiscent of a shady used-car lot. This isn’t just a shame—it’s an outright betrayal of trust. Save your money and invest in a grill that doesn’t require constant babysitting or an engineering degree to fix.
Results.Title: A price vs. customer service mismatch…

Today I had the misfortune of experiencing a disastrous unboxing and assembly process with my new Traeger Timberline grill. The assembly process took about 90 minutes (pretty straight forward), but when I finally plugged it in, the unit was dead on arrival—the display didn't turn on at all. To resolve the issue, I spent another 90 minutes waiting on hold for a Traeger Support technician.  Once connected, we spent another hour troubleshooting the issue together. This process was somewhat tedious, as it involved disconnecting numerous small connectors from the controller board and wire harness. Unfortunately, the call concluded with them deciding to send me a new hopper assembly containing all the electronics.

While I understand that parts may take some time to arrive—about a week in this case—I'm deeply frustrated by being expected to perform what they describe as "self-repair." This is not what I anticipated when spending over $3,000 on this product. Although shipping and parts are covered under warranty, it feels like resolving this issue has become my responsibility rather than theirs.

Overall, my experience has been marred with disappointment and frustration, not only with the product's poor performance straight out of the box but also with the prospect of spending additional time replacing parts. I foresee wasting hours on a Saturday dealing with these issues, which is far from what I expected when purchasing this product.

Although any outdoor grill will take a bit longer to reach temp in colder weather, the Timberline is a fully insulated grill. Because of this, once the goal temperature has been achieved, it will be easier to maintain, even as the mercury level drops. However, we really don’t expect meat probes to properly measure inside of the barrel when using them as a test. Even regular oven thermometers are not designed to take into consideration the unique environment that is inside of a pellet grill, which the internal thermocouple is specifically designed to do. If you want to do an accuracy test, the easiest way is to simply turn on your Timberline from a cold start and compare the initial reading to the ambient air temperature. If it is within a reasonable range, then the grill is working correctly. If it's over 20 degrees off from the start, then we’ll want to look into it further. This includes checking the tip of the thermocouple for damaged, and verifying that the red protective cap was removed before the first use. But if this does not seem to be the case, or you want some help with the diagnosis, please call us at 1-800-TRAEGER, and one of our agents will go over everything with you to make sure that your Timberline is running exactly the way if should be, which also includes addressing any concerns that you have with the WiFi feature as well.

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thanks for reviewing the Timberline XL. Although pellets are the number one cause of temperature issues, please hold off on throwing them out until it can be confirmed that they are really the reason for your Timberline's performance. You can do a quick pellet test by breaking a few between your fingers and making sure that they snap cleanly in half, as opposed to crumbling, which is a pretty accurate indicator of their condition. And while maintenance can also be a factor, you likely already have this covered, especially on such a new grill. But as long as food is not in the grill during startup, airflow isn't being obstructed by pans close the interior walls, and the weather is not exceptionally windy, you shouldn't see more than a +/-25 degree variation in temperature. If none of the topics mentioned here are related to your situation, please give Customer Service a call at 1-800-TRAEGER. We might be missing something very basic that could make a big difference in the performance of your Timberline, and a quick phone call may be all it takes to get it corrected.

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thank you for your interest in the Traeger Timberline. Since pellet grills create heat exclusively with burning wood, any food cooked on them will be smoked in the process. While cooking at lower temperatures (225 degrees and below) will enhance the production of smoke, the Timberline series also comes with a Super Smoke feature, which is designed to infuse even more flavor into food by maintaining precision control of airflow to the fire. However, this does not meant that your Timberline will constantly produce thick, dark clouds of smoke, unless there is a problem with the wood being used. Pellet grills are well known for their ability to create thin, clean, 'blue smoke', which is the preferred type of smoke for cooking. But sometimes this can give the impression that the food is not being smoked since it is so different than what is typically seen from old style stick smokers. When the time comes for your next cook, please consider using lower temperatures, and even the Super Smoke function, so that you can see just how much flavor your Timberline can add to the food.

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thank you for reviewing the Timberline XL. Although all pellet grills can be expected to fluctuate a little due to the way they work, swings of up to 30 – 40 degrees are certainly excessive. Unless you are using the Super Smoke feature, which is more about maximizing smoke production than precise temperature control, the range should typically fall within 25 degrees in either direction, with the average still being very close to what the grill is set to. But if these extreme swings are occurring during normal cooking, then they should be correctable without much effort. The most common causes for this type of behavior on the new touchscreen versions of the Timberline (and Ironwood) are often related to an improperly installed firepot, outdated firmware, or using foil on the drip tray. However, if these have already been checked, or if you would just like some help checking them, please give Traeger Customer Service a call. One of our agents will go over everything mentioned above, and even some more unlikely possibilities if it turns out to be something else.
